script: Players who got sent to PRISON! Gheorghe Popescu, better known as Gica Popescu, was the captain of FC Barcelona and one of the greatest players Romania has ever produced. And after retiring, he stayed deeply connected to Romanian football. Between 1999 and 2005, he got involved in a scheme surrounding 12 different player-transfers from Romanian clubs to foreign clubs. But this wasn't some behind-the-scenes disagreement over agent fees. When Paul Codrea got transferred from Dinamo București to Genoa in 2001, the Italian club paid $2.56 million, but Dinamo București reported that they received 70,000. When Florin Bratu got transferred to Galatasaray, the Turkish club paid 2.75 million, but Rapid București reported 100,000. The money that wasn't being reported was funneled through offshore companies, and Popescu was right in the middle of all of it. Prosecutors estimated that the state lost 1.7 million euros in taxes, while clubs lost around 10 million euros total. And in 2014, Romania's Court of Appeal sentenced Popescu to 3 years and 1 month in prison for tax evasion and money-laundering. He originally had a suspended sentence, meaning he wouldn't have served any time, but he appealed, and the appeals court came back even harder and gave him actual prison time. But here's a detail that makes the story unforgettable. That sentence was handed down on March 4th, and the election for the president of the Romanian Football Association was scheduled for March 5th. He was the favorite to win it.
